title: Questioning Coaching
author: Carousel Teaching
summary: Instructional coaching is well-evidenced in research but faces substantial implementation challenges that schools often underestimate. The core problems are psychological, structural, and practical: creating a two-tier teacher system generates discomfort and status anxiety; the term 'instructional coaching' lacks consistent definition across training providers, resulting in incoherent programs; implementation demands expert observers and significant budgets; and there is no consensus on what constitutes good teaching. Teachers elevated to coaching roles may be excellent practitioners yet lack coaching skill—two very different competencies. The research shows that the most effective coaching approach differs markedly depending on the target teacher's expertise level, yet schools rarely differentiate. Before committing to instructional coaching, schools must honestly assess whether it fits their culture, capacity, and current needs. Rushing into the model without addressing foundational questions leads to wasted investment and staff demoralization.
points: Instructional coaching creates psychological discomfort by designing a two-tier system where some teachers are positioned as experts and others as novices
The term instructional coaching lacks clear definition across training providers, leading to incoherent implementation and confusion
Full-scale instructional coaching costs approximately £86,700 annually per secondary school (roughly 1.7 additional teachers' salaries)
Effective coaching requires coaches who are expert observers able to perceive subtle teaching elements that casual observers miss
Instructional coaching works best with early-career or struggling teachers; it can slow down already-expert teachers who need different feedback
quotes: The relationship between coach and coachee is central to success in instructional coaching.
Many schools have not adequately thought through the two-tiered system they are creating when implementing coaching.
What passes for instructional coaching varies wildly from program to program across the country.
The effectiveness of coaching depends greatly on the expertise level of the teacher being coached.
Schools need to be honest about whether instructional coaching actually fits their cultural and structural context.” Archived from Carousel Teaching on April 20, 2026 by Tim.
